name: Task_3
description:
Finetune the MACE-MP-0b machine learning interatomic potential for a diatomic Ag₂ system. First, generate a dataset of Ag₂ configurations using an interatomic-distance grid spanning from 0.6 Å to 5.0 Å with a uniform spacing of 0.1 Å. Use the base MACE-MP foundation model as an ASE calculator to compute the potential energies and forces for all configurations, and store these as proxy labels. Next, use these generated pseudo-labels to fine-tune the MACE-MP-0b foundation model. Once fine-tuning is complete, load the resulting checkpoint as an ASE calculator. Construct a conventional cubic FCC unit cell of Silver (4 Ag atoms) and expand it into a 3×3×3 supercell (108 atoms). Perform a molecular dynamics (MD) simulation on this supercell at 300 K for 5 ps, choosing a Langevin or NVTBerendsen thermostat, integration timestep, and regular trajectory sampling sufficient to resolve motion. Submit the labeled dataset, trained checkpoint, trajectory, and calculation log in the format specified below.

Use isolated, nonperiodic dimers, the supplied teacher.model (MACE-MP-0) with dispersion for the proxy labels, and student.model (MACE-MP-0b) as the starting checkpoint; run bulk MD without dispersion at a fixed lattice parameter of 4.09 Å. The evaluator derives training-set energy RMSE per atom and force-component RMSE before and after fitting. Initialize velocities once at 300 K with a recorded seed and remove center-of-mass momentum once. Retain the bulk trajectory so the evaluator can derive its temperature, energy, force, displacement, and pair-distance diagnostics. Poor transfer or structural evolution is a valid result, but must be distinguished from numerical integration failure.
